title: Religion Is a Team Sport
coreMove: Evaluate religion by the team behavior it organizes as well as by the beliefs it states.
sourcePressure: The chapter interprets religion as a group-binding institution that coordinates ritual, cohesion, and shared moral life without reducing religion to one function.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The writer argues for or against religion's truth instead of analyzing its coordinating function.

sourceAnchors.name: Religion Is a Team Sport
sourceAnchors.detail: the official index title and sidecar frame religion as group-binding technology rather than only private belief.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Religion here is not only a claim in the head; it is a set of shared moves that makes people act like a team.

sourceAnchors.name: the hive switch
sourceAnchors.detail: the frozen sidecar says Chapter 11 builds on Chapter 10's hive-switch mechanism.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Ritual matters because it can reach for the same switch that makes separate people move as one body.

hook: Do not open ch11 with a person discovering that morality is complicated.
Do not use 'you think X, but actually Y' as the hook shell.
counterintuition: Avoid treating the opposing view as stupid before explaining the mechanism.
tryThisNow: No generic write down your values prompt.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm - a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.domain: synagogue meal train after a family funeral
exampleSpecs.audience: readers seeing ritual as coordinated care
exampleSpecs.stakes: Michael notices belief, schedule, food, and duty forming one team response.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Michael watches the signup sheet fill before anyone asks whether the grieving family needs help.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Foil-covered pans line the community room counter beside a handwritten signup sheet.

exampleSpecs.domain: secular recovery group borrowing ritual structure
exampleSpecs.stakes: Lin sees repeated words and chairs create accountability beyond private resolve.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Lin changes the meeting from advice swapping to a shared opening and commitment round.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Same words, same chairs, every week," Lin says, setting the circle.

exampleSpecs.domain: church youth group organizing flood cleanup
exampleSpecs.stakes: Chloe treats prayer, vans, and work gloves as one coordination system.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Chloe pairs the spoken blessing with named crews and departure times so warmth becomes action.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Work gloves are piled beneath the fellowship hall clock.

exampleSpecs.domain: mosque committee resolving a donation dispute
exampleSpecs.audience: lay leaders protecting trust in sacred giving
exampleSpecs.stakes: Tomas sees the ritual of transparent counting as team trust, not mere accounting.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Tomas introduces two-person counting in public view after hearing suspicion spread.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Tomas one whispered accusation to see that trust needed a ritual, not a spreadsheet.

exampleSpecs.domain: interfaith hospital chaplaincy coordinating bedside coverage
exampleSpecs.audience: care teams supporting families under stress
exampleSpecs.stakes: Nina maps how shared sacred duty makes strangers cover hard hours.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Nina read the coverage board as a moral team, not a staffing puzzle.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You see a chapel light still on after midnight beside the coverage board.

exampleSpecs.domain: Buddhist meditation center handling a member's illness
exampleSpecs.audience: small spiritual communities converting practice into support
exampleSpecs.stakes: Vincent notices chanting, rides, and meals binding separate households.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Which part of Vincent's community response would disappear if practice stayed private?
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What changes when silence on a cushion becomes a rota on the fridge?

skillTargets: evaluate religion as social coordination without reducing it to that alone
connect ritual to cohesion and shared moral life
see both binding and blinding effects of sacred community

tryThisNowSpec: Look at one ritual you know and list the team behaviors it organizes: showing up, giving, singing, eating, mourning, forgiving.
